deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.4-6): Grothendieck is building a topos-theoretic mapping cylinder in order to do homotopy theory of topoi (weak equivalences tested by cohomology and locally constant coefficients). The aim is to relate this to Top(X) for small categories X, in the spirit of Pursuing Stacks and the modelizer programme.

On p.4 he records the setup. Giving a geometric morphism f: X_0 -> X_1 is the same as giving a topos X with an open subtopos X_0 and its closed complement X_1. The recollement (gluing) functor phi = i_1^* j_{0*}: F(X_0) -> F(X_1) must commute with all limits, so that phi = f_* has a left adjoint f^*, and f^* must be left exact. Then X is the Artin gluing Gl(f_*), whose objects are triples (F_0, F_1, u: F_1 -> f_*F_0). There is a retraction p: X -> X_1 with p^*F_1 = (f^*F_1, F_1, unit). Since Gamma(X,(F_0,F_1,u)) = Gamma(X_1,F_1), the relative cohomology sequence (S) becomes (S'), with H^i(X,F) replaced by H^i(X_1,F_1).

This page (p.5):

(1) The first claim reads: "f: X_0 -> X_1 is [asphérique, crossed out; replaced by a word read as équi-fidèle] iff the open inclusion X_0 -> X is." The reason is that X_1 -> X is a homotopy equivalence, with retraction p and p∘i = id. Hence X_0 -> X factors as i∘f up to this equivalence, and any property invariant under composition with weak equivalences transfers.

(2) NB: the locally constant sheaves on X are exactly the triples (F_1, f^*F_1, tautological u) with F_1 locally constant on X_1, i.e. p^*F_1. So LC(X) ≃ LC(X_1). This is what makes (1) work for a fidelity property of pullback on locally constant sheaves (pi_0/pi_1-type Galois conditions): f^* on LC is fully faithful or an equivalence iff j_0^* is.

(3) Part 2 starts the converse direction. Take a topos X and an open subtopos X_0. This is the same as a subobject of the final object e_X, and it determines the residual closed topos X_1. Equivalently, it is a geometric morphism pi: X -> Top(Delta_1), where Top(Delta_1) is the presheaf topos on the arrow category, i.e. the Sierpinski topos, which classifies subterminal objects. X_0 is the inverse image of the universal open point {0}, and X_1 that of the closed point {1}.

The next page says (X, X_0) is the same as a triple (X_0, X_1, phi) with phi left exact and accessible. It then asks for conditions making both inclusions X_0 -> X <- X_1 weak equivalences. It notes that f^* need not be left exact for this, and then specialises to X = Top(X) for X a category over Delta_1.
errors: No mathematical error. The first line as transcribed ('f: X_1 -> X_1') must mean f: X_0 -> X_1; this is a reading issue.

I checked the NB. Take a covering (U^a) of e_X on which F is constant. Since f^*U_1^a -> U_0^a and the f^*U_1^a cover X_0, the adjoint map f^*F_1 -> F_0 is locally an isomorphism, hence an isomorphism. The NB is correct for any geometric morphism f; no left-exactness beyond that of f^* is needed.
The equivalence in (1) tacitly uses that X_1 -> X is a weak equivalence. That holds by the retraction p (a homotopy of topoi via Top(Delta_1)), but it is not proved on the page.
The prose phrase 'Les X_1 faisceaux' is probably a mis-reading of 'Les faisceaux'; it is not a mathematical point.

ideas.what: Gluing a topos along f_* (open X_0, closed X_1) as the mapping cylinder of a geometric morphism f: X_0 -> X_1, with retraction onto X_1
ideas.modern_name: Artin gluing / recollement; topos mapping cylinder (cocomma object of topoi)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin, Grothendieck, Verdier (SGA4 IV §9.5, 1963-64); Wraith; Johnstone (Topos Theory, 1977)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV §9.5 (recollement); the mapping-cylinder interpretation is unsure

ideas.what: Locally constant sheaves on the glued topos Gl(f_*) are exactly pullbacks p^*F_1 of locally constant sheaves on the closed part
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy invariance of local systems under deformation retraction (mapping cylinder)

ideas.what: A property of f (asphericity, or fidelity on locally constant sheaves) holds iff it holds for the open inclusion X_0 -> X
ideas.modern_name: 2-out-of-3 for weak equivalences applied to the cylinder factorisation

ideas.what: Open subtopos = subterminal object = geometric morphism to Top(Delta_1), the Sierpinski topos, with X_0 and X_1 as inverse images of the open and closed points
ideas.modern_name: Sierpinski topos classifies subterminals; stratification of a topos over the poset [1]
ideas.where_published: SGA4 IV 9.4 has open/closed subtopoi; the Top(Delta_1) formulation is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a recollement as a morphism pi: X -> Top(Delta_1) and studies when the strata inclusions are weak equivalences. Together with p.6, where X = Top(X) with X a category over Delta_1, this anticipates treating stratified topoi over a poset and their homotopy theory via categories over the poset. This is the setting later developed as exodromy / stratified ∞-topoi (Lurie HA App. A; Barwick-Glasman-Haine). The mapping-cylinder case phi = f_* is the case where the 'link' collapses onto X_0.
missed.quote: la donnée de X_0 correspond ... celle d'une application π: X → Top(Δ_1), X_0 étant l'image inverse du sous-topos ouvert "universel" {0}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it places an early homotopy-theoretic use of stratifications over Delta_1 in Grothendieck's 1980s notes. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but standard material: Artin gluing as a mapping cylinder, local systems pulled back from the closed stratum, and the Sierpinski-topos classification of open subtopoi. The only mild interest is the early homotopy-of-topoi framing via Top(Delta_1), which foreshadows stratified-topos methods.
